- When sentiment turns positive (≥ 0.33) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤ 0.00) for 5+ days, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (especially days 1–7); apply 1–3% downward bias for first 7 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–70), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true values.  
- When sentiment history shows increasing positivity (e.g., 0.00 → 0.33 → 0.50), model often fails to capture momentum; apply 1–2% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
